Rashi on Niddah 27b:10:1.english: They said the same thing - And later, we establish that [the ruling] of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov is due to nullification in a majority.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:10:2.english: A large animal - That had never had an offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:10:3.hebrew: תקבר - החררה, שהוא מיחוי של בכור:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:10:3.english: Must be buried - [This refers to] the mass [of blood], which is the dissolved remains of a firstborn.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:10:4.hebrew: ופטורה מן הבכורה - שאם תלד עוד, אין ולדה לכהן:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:10:4.english: And is exempt from the firstborn - That if it gives birth again, its offspring is not [given] to the priest.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:11:1.english: It does not impart ritual impurity - [This refers to] that mass [of congealed blood].

Rashi on Niddah 27b:11:2.hebrew: ומאחר דאינה מטמאה - אלמא לא חיישינן לולד, אמאי תקבר:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:11:2.english: And since it does not impart impurity - Evidently we are not concerned that there is a fetus; why [then] must it be buried?

Rashi on Niddah 27b:11:3.hebrew: ומשני כדי לפרסמה - שנפטרה מן הבכורה, שידעו הכל שזה פטר רחם:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:11:3.english: And [the Gemara] answers: In order to publicize it - That she has become exempt from [the law of] the firstborn, so that everyone will know that this opened the womb.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:12:1.hebrew: ופרכינן: מדפטורה מן הבכורה, אלמא ולד מעליא היא, אמאי אינה מטמאה:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:12:1.english: And we object: Since [the animal] is exempt from the firstborn, evidently [the mass] is a full-fledged offspring; why does it not impart impurity?

Rashi on Niddah 27b:12:2.english: Nullification in a majority - The dissolved substance of the fetus is nullified in the blood.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:13:1.hebrew: ומודה ר"ש - במתני' בשליא, אע"ג שהבית טהור, אמו טמאה לידה:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:13:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon concedes - In the mishna regarding an afterbirth, that even though the house is pure, its mother is impure [with the impurity of] childbirth.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:14:1.english: Similar to what she emitted as seed - That is to say, that it liquefied like semen.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:15:1.hebrew: שטרפוהו - כמו (חולין סד.) ביצים טרופות בקערה, שמחקוהו ובלבלוהו:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:15:1.english: That they scrambled it - As in (Chullin 64a), "eggs beaten in a bowl" — [meaning] that they mashed it and mixed it up.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:15:2.english: In its fluids - That they rinsed it in them. Alternatively, in the fluids of birth and the discharge that emerge with it.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:16:1.hebrew: שנתבלבלה - נמחק כולו, כמו שרוף שנתפזר ואין שלדו קיימת:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:16:1.english: [Whose form] became distorted - It was completely obliterated, like a burned [corpse] that was scattered and its skeletal frame is not intact.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:16:2.hebrew: ושלדו קיימת - גופו קיים, שלא נתפזר האפר, ועדיין נראה כשלם:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:16:2.english: And its skeleton remains intact - Its body is intact, in that the ash was not scattered, and it still appears whole.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:2:1.english: Its end - [The end] of corpse mold is like its beginning.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:2:2.hebrew: מה תחלתו - כשנקבר, אם יש דבר הראוי לירקב ולעשות רקב של מת:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:2:2.english: Just as in its initial state - When [the corpse] is buried, if there is an item fit to decompose and produce decay [along with that] of the corpse.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:2:3.hebrew: גנגילון - בטול, שאותו דבר אחר מבטלו. אף סופו, לאחר שנעשה רקב כשנקבר כהלכתו, ד"א המתערבת בו מבטלו. ולשון גנגילון: דבר העומד כנגדו לבטלו ולקלקלו. ולקמן פריך: הואיל וטעמא דר"ש ברקב כדאמר השתא, גבי שליא, דליכא למימר הכי, מ"ט:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:2:3.english: Gangilon - Nullification; [meaning] that that other matter nullifies it. So too in its ultimate state, after it has become corpse dust [rekav] when buried in accordance with halakha, another matter that is mixed into it nullifies it. And the expression "gangilon" [denotes] a thing that stands against it [kenegdo] to nullify it and spoil it. And later [on 27b], [the Gemara] challenges: Since the reason of Rabbi Shimon regarding corpse dust is as [Rabba] said now, with regard to an afterbirth, where this cannot be said, what is the reason [for his ruling]?

Rashi on Niddah 27b:3:1.english: What is it - [Regarding that] which [Rabba] said: "[In] its initial state, another matter becomes a nullification [gangilon] for it."

Rashi on Niddah 27b:3:2.english: That does not have corpse-dust - That its corpse-dust does not impart impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:3:3.english: Naked in a marble coffin or on a stone floor - For in this case, there is no admixture in its decay.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:4:1.hebrew: נקבר בכסותו - דאיכא רקבובית, או אפילו ערום בארון של עץ, דאיכא רקבובית:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:4:1.english: [If] he was buried in his garment - For there is decayed matter [of the garment], or even [if he was] naked in a wooden coffin, as there is decayed matter [of the wood].

Rashi on Niddah 27b:4:2.english: Or on a brick floor - For their earth dissolves.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:4:3.english: That does not have corpse-dust - Because of another substance mixed into it.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:4:4.hebrew: לאפוקי הרוג דלא - לפי שיצא דמו וחסר, וקיימא לן במס' נזיר (דף נא.), מת שחסר אין לו רקב:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:4:4.english: To exclude one who was killed, who does not - Because his blood flowed out and he is incomplete, and we hold in Tractate Nazir (page 51a) [that] an incomplete corpse does not have [the status of] corpse dust.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:5:1.english: That was scattered within the house, [the house] is impure - Because of a tent.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:6:1.hebrew: דאין מאהיל וחוזר ומאהיל - גג שכנגד זה מאהיל על חצי שיעור, ושכנגד זה מאהיל על חצי שיעור, ושני אהלות הן, ואין מצטרפין:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:6:1.english: That it does not overshadow and overshadow again - The roof that is opposite this [portion] overshadows half the required measure, and that which is opposite that [portion] overshadows half the required measure, and they are two [separate] tents, and they do not combine.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:8:1.hebrew: מלא תרוד ועוד - יותר ממלא תרוד עפר בית הקברות. ל"א: רקב ממש של מת, אלא כגון שנקבר בכסותו או בקרקע בלא ארון של שיש, ויש כאן מלא תרוד ועוד מאותו עפר, דהוו מעורבין רקב ועפר:
Rashi on Niddah 27b:8:1.english: A ladleful and more - More than a ladleful of cemetery earth. Another explanation: [It is] actual corpse dust of a deceased person, but [in a case] such as where he was buried in his garment or in the ground without a marble coffin, and there is a ladleful and more of that earth here, as corpse dust and earth were mixed together.

Rashi on Niddah 27b:9:1.english: Nullified by a majority - That the blood of childbirth was more abundant than the dissolved fetus and nullifies it.

Tosafot on Niddah 27b:11:1.hebrew: כדי לפרסמה שפטורה - הא דתנן בפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עז.), מבכרת שהפילה שליא ישליכנה לכלבים — התם א"צ פרסום, דהכל יודעים שיש ולד בשליא:
Tosafot on Niddah 27b:11:1.english: In order to publicize that [the animal] is exempt - [As for] that which we learned in the chapter of "Behema HaMaksheh" (Chullin 77a), "[In the case of] a first-calving animal that discharged an afterbirth, one may cast it to the dogs" — there, it does not require publicity, for everyone knows that there is an offspring in an afterbirth.

Tosafot on Niddah 27b:12:1.hebrew: משום בטול ברוב נגעו בה - וא"ת: דבבכורות פרק הלוקח בהמה (בכורות כג.) גבי נבלה בטלה בשחוטה, וקאמר: אין מטמאה במגע אבל מטמאה במשא, דטומאה כמאן דאיתא דמיא; ופריך מחררת דם, דאינה מטמאה לא במגע ולא במשא משום בטול ברוב, אלמא דכמאן דליתיה דמיא; ומשני: משום דה"ל טומאה סרוחה; ופריך: הניחא לבר פדא דדריש עד לגר, אלא לר' דדריש עד לכלב, קשיא. ואמאי לא מקשה מהך דשפיר, דאינו מטמא באהל משום בטול ברוב, אלמא כמאן דליתיה דמי; והשתא לא מצי לשנויי משום דהוי טומאה סרוחה, דאפילו מת סרוח מטמא? וי"ל: משום דאיכא למדחי דטעמא משום בילבול צורה כדר"ל, ולא משום בטול ברוב. אי נמי, כיון דטעמא דשפיר משום מת שלם, אע"ג דטומאה כמאן דאיתיה דמי, אין להחשיבו שלם, כיון שנתבטל ברוב לגמרי:
Tosafot on Niddah 27b:12:1.english: Due to nullification in a majority they touched upon it - And if you say: In Bekhorot, in the chapter [entitled] HaLokei'ach Behemah (Bekhorot 23a), regarding an animal carcass [neveilah] that is nullified in [meat of] a slaughtered animal [shechutah], and it says [that] it does not impart impurity through contact, but it imparts impurity through carrying, for the impurity is considered as though it exists; and it objects from [the baraita of] a mass of blood [chararat dam], which does not impart impurity, neither through contact nor through carrying, because of nullification in a majority, evidently [showing that] it is considered as though it does not exist; and it answers: Because it is decayed impurity [tum'ah seruchah]; and it objects: This works out well according to Bar Padda, who expounds "until [it is unfit for] a resident alien (ger)" [Deuteronomy 14:21], but according to Rabbi [Yoḥanan], who expounds "until [it is unfit for] a dog", it is difficult — [if so,] why does [the Gemara in Bekhorot] not object from this [case] of a gestational sac [shafir], which does not impart impurity in a tent [ohel] because of nullification in a majority, evidently [proving that] it is considered as though it does not exist? And now, it could not answer that it is because it is decayed impurity, for even a decayed corpse imparts impurity! And one can say: Because one could deflect [the objection by arguing] that the reason is due to deformation of form, in accordance with [the view of] Reish Lakish, and not because of nullification in a majority. Alternatively: Since the reason [for impurity in the case] of a gestational sac is because of [the status of] a complete corpse, even though the impurity is considered as though it exists, one cannot consider it complete, since it has been completely nullified in the majority.

Tosafot on Niddah 27b:16:1.hebrew: מת שנתבלבלה צורתו מנלן דטהור - וקשה: מאי פריך ליה ר' יוחנן? האמר בסמוך דר' יוחנן כר"א, וא"כ ר"ל ניחא טפי, דקאי כרבנן, דקתני במסכת אהלות: "וחכמים מטהרים"?! וי"ל, דר"י ור"ל אליבא דרבנן פליגי: דר"ל סבר, דלרבנן דמטהרי ברובע, ה"נ דמטהרי אפילו בשלם, בשאין שלדו קיימת ונתבלבל צורתו; אבל שלדו קיימת טמאה מדרבי יצחק, דאתיא כרבנן, דאי כר"א, אפי' אין שלדו קיימת טמא, דהא מטמא ר"א ברובע של אפר. וא"ל לר' יוחנן: מנלן הא דרבנן מטהרו משום בלבול צורה? דלמא טעמא דרבנן דכשנשרף אין עוד שם מת עליו, אפילו כולו שלם ושלדו קיימת; אבל שפיר, שם מת עליו וטמא, אי לאו משום דבטל ברוב. ומילתא דרבי יצחק לא אתיא כרבנן, אלא כר"א, דמטמא מת שרוף וחסר, ושלדו קיימת נקט לטהר פתחים קטנים. א"נ, קסבר ר' יוחנן דרבנן לא מטהרי אלא ברובע דחסר, אבל אם העפר שלם, אפי' אין שלדו קיימת טמא. והשתא אתי שפיר, שא"צ לחלק בין שפיר ושליא למת שנשרף ואין שלדו קיימת, דשניהם שוין לר"ל ולר' יוחנן. ובירושלמי איכא: שפיר שנתבלבל צורתו מהו? ר' יוחנן אמר טמא, ר"ל אמר טהור. איתיביה ר"ל לר' יוחנן מרבי יצחק מגדלאה, ומשני: דבר תורה אפילו שלדו קיימת טהורה, מפני מה אמרו טמא? מפני כבודו. פירוש: מפני כבודו של מת הוא דלא בטל. וזהו כפירוש ראשון, דאף בשלדו קיימת טהור דבר תורה, וחולק על הגמרא שלנו דמוקי לה כר"א מילתא דרבי יצחק, והתם מוקי לה כרבנן:
Tosafot on Niddah 27b:16:1.english: A corpse whose form was deformed, from where do we [derive] that it is pure? - And it is difficult: What is Rabbi Yoḥanan challenging him? Doesn't [the Gemara] say nearby that Rabbi Yoḥanan [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer? And if so, Reish Lakish is even better [situated], as he stands in accordance with the Rabbis, where it is taught in tractate Oholot: "And the Sages deem pure"?! And one can say that Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish disagree according to [the view of] the Rabbis: For Reish Lakish maintains that according to the Rabbis, who deem pure [ashes] in [the measure of] a quarter[-kav], so too do they deem pure even [in the case of] a complete [corpse], when its skeleton does not remain and its form was deformed; but [if] its skeleton remains, it is impure based on [the statement of] Rabbi Yitzḥak, which goes according to the Rabbis; for if [it were] according to Rabbi Eliezer, even [if] its skeleton does not remain it would be impure, since Rabbi Eliezer deems impure [even] a quarter[-kav] of ashes. And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan: From where do we [derive] this, that the Rabbis deem pure due to deformation of form? Perhaps the reasoning of the Rabbis is that once [a corpse] is burned, the designation of a corpse is no longer upon it, even [if] it is entirely complete and its skeleton remains; but [regarding] a gestational sac, the designation of a corpse is upon it, and it would be impure were it not for [the fact] that it is nullified in the majority. And the statement of Rabbi Yitzḥak does not go according to the Rabbis, but rather according to Rabbi Eliezer, who deems impure a corpse that is burned and deficient; and he mentioned "and its skeleton remains" to deem pure the small openings. Alternatively, Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains that the Rabbis deem pure only in [the case of] a quarter[-kav] where it is deficient, but if the dust is complete, even [if] its skeleton does not remain, it is impure. And now it works out well, that there is no need to distinguish between a gestational sac or placenta and a corpse that was burned and its skeleton does not remain, for both are equivalent according to Reish Lakish and according to Rabbi Yoḥanan. And in the Yerushalmi there is [the following discussion]: A gestational sac whose form was deformed, what is [its status]? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Impure. Reish Lakish said: Pure. Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yoḥanan from [the statement of] Rabbi Yitzḥak Migdala'ah, and he answered: By Torah law, even [if] its skeleton remains it is pure; why did they say [it is] impure? Because of its dignity. Explanation: It is because of the dignity of the deceased that it is not nullified. And this is like the first explanation, that even when its skeleton remains it is pure by Torah law; and it disagrees with our Gemara, which establishes the statement of Rabbi Yitzḥak in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, whereas there [in the Yerushalmi], it establishes it in accordance with the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Niddah 27b:2:1.hebrew: גלגילון - פירש בערוך: דבר הנגלל עמו:
Tosafot on Niddah 27b:2:1.english: Galgeilon - It is explained in the Arukh: Something that is rolled with it.

Tosafot on Niddah 27b:4:1.hebrew: למעוטי הרוג - דמחוסר דם. והא דאמר עולא בפ' כ"ג (נזיר נא.), אין רקב למת אלא לבא מן הבשר, מן הגידין ומן העצמות — א"כ משמע דאין רקב טמא אא"כ בא משלשתן יחד, אבל רקב מדם לא בעי; מ"מ, אם חסר מדמו בשעה שנקבר, אין לו דין רקב:
Tosafot on Niddah 27b:4:1.english: To exclude one who was killed - For he is lacking blood. And as for that which Ulla said in the chapter [entitled] "Kohen Gadol" (Nazir 51a), "There is no dust for a corpse except that which comes from the flesh, from the sinews, and from the bones" — if so, this implies that dust is not impure unless it comes from [all] three of them together, but dust from blood is not required; nevertheless, if he was lacking [any] of his blood at the time he was buried, he does not have the law of dust.

Tosafot on Niddah 27b:8:1.hebrew: מלא תרוד ועוד - פ"ה: כגון שנקבר בכסותו. ואין נראה לרשב"ם, דבתחלה מודו כ"ע דדבר אחר נעשה לו גלגילון. ונראה לרשב"ם, דהכא מיירי בנקבר ערום, ודרכן היה לטוח כוכין בסיד, ומיד שנתרקב היה התרוד ממנו טמא, ואח"כ נפל מן הסיד ונתערבה עם הרקב שכבר היה טמא. ומהך לא עביד צריכותא דקמ"ל, משום דא"א שלא יהא תרוד מרקב קודם שנתערב בו עפר:
Tosafot on Niddah 27b:8:1.english: A ladleful and more - Rashi explains: Such as where he was buried in his clothing. But this does not appear [correct] to the Rashbam, for initially, everyone agrees that another substance becomes a nullification [gilgilon] to it. And it appears to the Rashbam that here it is dealing with [a case where] he was buried naked, and it was their practice to plaster [burial] niches with lime; and as soon as it decomposed, the ladleful [of decay] from it was impure, and afterward [some] of the lime fell and became mixed with the decay, which had already become impure. And from this [baraita, the Gemara] does not construct a tzerikhuta [to show what novelty] it teaches us, because [what it comes to teach us is] that it is impossible that there would not be a ladleful of decay before dirt became mixed into it.
